cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: So Luke, for our next psychology assignment we have to do something on sleep and dreams.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: Right.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: I've just read an article suggesting why we tend to forget most of our dreams soon after

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: we wake up.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: I mean, most of my dreams aren't that interesting anyway, but what it said was that if we

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: remembered everything, we might get mixed up about what actually happened and what we

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: dreamed. So it's a sort of protection. I hadn't heard that idea before.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: I'd always assumed that it was just that we didn't have room in our memories for all that

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: stuff.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: Me too. What do you think about the idea that our dreams may predict the future?

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: Yeah, lots of people have a story of it happening to them, but the explanation I've read

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: is that for each dream that comes true, we have thousands that don't, but we don't notice

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: those, we don't even remember them.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: We just remember the ones where something in the real world, like a view or an action,

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: happens to trigger a dream memory.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: Right. So it's just a coincidence really.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: Something else I read about is what they call segmented sleeping.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: That's a theory that hundreds of years ago, people used to get up in the middle of the

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: night and have a chat or something to eat, then go back to bed. So I tried it myself.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: Well it's meant to make you more creative. I don't know why.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: But I gave it up after a week. It just didn't fit in with my lifestyle.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: But most pre-school children have a short sleep in the day don't they?

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: There was an experiment some students did here last term to see at what age kids should

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: stop having naps. But they didn't really find an answer.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: They spent a lot of time working out the most appropriate methodology, but the results

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: didn't seem to show any obvious patterns.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: Right. Anyway, let's think about our assignment.

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: Last time I had problems with the final stage, where we had to describe and justify how

cues.speaker: KE
cues.text: successful we thought we'd been. I struggled a bit with the action plan too.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: I was OK with the planning, but I got marked down for the self-assessment as well.

cues.speaker: IE
cues.text: And I had big problems with the statistical stuff, that's where I really lost marks.
